# EEZ Quickstarts

> Fourteen interactive walkthroughs of the Ethereum Economic Zone, each built on real
> protocol source cited at a pinned commit rather than on pseudocode. Covers writing
> contracts that call across rollups, running the stack, and how Rollup0 settles and proves.

Every code panel on this site is rendered from JavaScript at runtime, so fetching a page
gives you the shell and not the content. These files hand over the content directly: each
walkthrough's narration and code, the full compilable Solidity behind the Solidity ones,
and the runnable Foundry tests.

Two things worth knowing before you use any of it. EEZ is pre-mainnet, so treat
capability claims as design intent rather than shipped behaviour; the proof system in the
public source is dev-grade ECDSA, not production ZK. And every citation here is pinned to
a commit SHA, so a link tells you exactly which revision a claim was true of.

## Dapp developers

Writing contracts that call across rollups.

- [Compute your cross-chain address](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q1-compute-your-cross-chain-address.html): Every contract gets one deterministic address on every other rollup.
- [Send a cross-chain call](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q2-send-a-cross-chain-call.html): Call the proxy like a normal contract — EEZ handles the routing.
- [How msg.sender resolves across chains](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q3-fix-the-msg-sender-gotcha.html): The destination always sees the proxy, never your original address.
- [How the proxy registry works](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q4-check-if-an-address-is-a-proxy.html): Every real proxy is recorded on-chain, and anyone can read it directly.
- [Encode a call's content hash](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q5-encode-a-calls-content-hash.html): Reorder the fields and you get a silently different hash.
- [Why the manager only accepts proxy calls](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q6-why-you-cant-call-the-manager-directly.html): Direct calls revert — only a registered proxy reaches execution.

## Rollup operators

Standing the stack up and driving it.

- [Run the EEZ devnet with Kurtosis](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro1-run-the-devnet-with-kurtosis.html): One command: sequencer, composer, proof-signer, embedded L1.
- [Deploy the protocol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro2-deploy-the-protocol.html): One script: EEZ, the proof system, and your manager.
- [Run the Chiado L2](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro3-run-a-real-chiado-l2.html): Same stack, a real testnet instead of a sandbox.
- [Send & test cross-chain calls](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro4-send-and-test-cross-chain-calls.html): Two ports, four op types, real pass/fail metrics.

## Protocol researchers

How Rollup0 actually settles and proves.

- [The four components of Rollup0](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr1-the-four-components-of-rollup0.html): Sequencer, composer, proof-signer, deriver — who does what.
- [Commit-first, repair-if-needed](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr2-commit-first-repair-if-needed.html): L2 commits immediately. L1 is still the source of truth.
- [The deriver: rebuilding L2 state from L1 alone](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr3-the-deriver.html): Rebuild the whole L2 chain from L1 alone.
- [How the composer proves a batch](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr4-how-the-composer-proves-a-batch.html): One gRPC stream: header, then blocks, then a signature.

## Compilable source

Real files, not fragments: pragma, imports and a contract wrapper, all building under solc 0.8.28. Each mirrors the upstream function its walkthrough cites.

- [snippets/q1-compute-address.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q1-compute-address.sol): full source behind Compute your cross-chain address
- [snippets/q2-cross-chain-call.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q2-cross-chain-call.sol): full source behind Send a cross-chain call
- [snippets/q3-msg-sender.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q3-msg-sender.sol): full source behind How msg.sender resolves across chains
- [snippets/q4-proxy-registry.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q4-proxy-registry.sol): full source behind How the proxy registry works
- [snippets/q5-content-hash.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q5-content-hash.sol): full source behind Encode a call's content hash
- [snippets/q6-manager-direct.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q6-manager-direct.sol): full source behind Why the manager only accepts proxy calls

## Runnable tests

Foundry tests with no forge-std and no submodules, so they drop into an existing suite. `cd snippets && forge test`.

- [snippets/test/Q3MsgSender.t.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/test/Q3MsgSender.t.sol): proves the behaviour in How msg.sender resolves across chains
- [snippets/test/Q5ContentHash.t.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/test/Q5ContentHash.t.sol): proves the behaviour in Encode a call's content hash
- [snippets/test/Q6ManagerDirect.t.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/test/Q6ManagerDirect.t.sol): proves the behaviour in Why the manager only accepts proxy calls
